items.name: Slope at 240 m and 570 m

items.status_note: Both slopes enter the score.
items.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters

items.name: Roughness at 200 m
items.plain: Small-scale elevation variability in the model.
items.status_note: Enters the score. The elevation models differ most at this roughness scale.
items.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters

items.name: Roughness at 400 to 1,600 m
items.plain: Elevation variability at three larger scales.
items.status_note: All three roughness values enter the score.
items.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters

items.name: Closed depression share
items.plain: Share of each cell occupied by closed depressions.
items.status_note: Enters the score.
items.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters

items.name: Closed depression depth
items.plain: Depth of the depressions detected by the same terrain algorithm.
items.status_note: Enters the score.
items.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters

items.name: Land cover
items.plain: Bare, ice and water shares constrain Earth eligibility.
items.status_note: Moss and lichen count as bare.

items.name: Elevation
items.plain: Median elevation of the Earth patch.
items.status_note: Shown for context; the score uses terrain shape.

items.name: Gentle slopes

items.status_note: Supports a landing and mobility comparison.

items.name: Total weighted patch area as primary rank
items.plain: The sum of the similarities over an entire patch.
items.status_note: The best window sets the rank to reduce the influence of patch size.
items.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters

items.name: Dune-like relief as a sand detector
items.plain: A rule based on the ratio of relief to roughness.
items.status_note: Temperature and moisture checks did not confirm dry sand. The flag remains a terrain rule.
items.dimension: Dust, wind, erosion and surface processes

items.name: Earth climatology
items.plain: NASA POWER skin temperature at the reanalysis grid scale.
items.status_note: Separate from the satellite measurements.

items.name: Midsummer solar elevation
items.plain: Estimated local noon Sun angle on Earth.
items.status_note: Reported as an environmental difference.

items.name: Air pressure
items.plain: Standard-atmosphere estimate from elevation.
items.status_note: Actual field pressure varies.

items.name: Measured Earth surface temperatures
items.plain: JAXA GCOM-C and MODIS day and night surface summaries.
items.status_note: Coverage and available months vary by site.

items.name: Soil moisture
items.plain: JAXA AMSR2 monthly soil moisture.
items.status_note: Available only where the product covers a sampled site.

items.name: Permafrost and ground temperature
items.plain: ESA CCI permafrost fraction and temperature at depth.
items.status_note: Available only for sampled coverage.

items.name: Lunar temperatures and ice stability
items.plain: Diviner surface temperatures and inferred stable ice depth.
items.status_note: Temperature and ice stability are different measurements and inferences.

items.name: Lunar shadow and visibility
items.plain: LOLA-derived permanent shadow and Sun and Earth visibility.
items.status_note: Reported for the lunar region.

items.name: Lunar radar, neutrons and ultraviolet
items.plain: Mini-RF, LEND and LAMP measurements.
items.status_note: These products describe the lunar region and do not enter the score.

items.name: Lunar terrain estimator
items.plain: Comparison with the published LOLA slope and roughness grids.
items.status_note: Check against a NASA product.

items.name: Known analogs and matched random circles
items.plain: Enrichment around documented sites and random locations.

items.status_note: The uncertainty interval includes chance.

items.name: Regolith chemistry

items.status_note: Requires different measurements.

criteria_note: Registry of analog criteria. Statuses come from the code and data of the repository, not from the plan; the proof of each status is in 'evidence' and in app/CRITERIA-NOTES.md. site_fields are dotted paths into one record of app/data/sites.json (and sites_flagged.json); moon_fields are dotted paths into one record of moon.json · regions (a named region; members only for base_regions). Ported from the J7 prototype and re-checked against the repository for J39 (issue #25); see app/CRITERIA-NOTES.md. Written with SI assistance (Claude Code).

criteria_statuses.mask: Precondition: a cell must pass it to be a candidate
criteria_statuses.context: Measured per site and shown, not scored
criteria_statuses.validation: Used to check the method, not part of the ranking
criteria_statuses.not_reproducible: No place on Earth reproduces it

dimensions: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
Dust, wind, erosion and surface processes
Landing, mobility, navigation, operations and construction

criteria_groups.name: Terrain shape in 3D
criteria_groups.summary: Quantities computed from elevation models by the same code on the Moon and on Earth. Three of them (roughness at four sizes, two-point slope at two baselines, closed depressions) make the eight numbers of the similarity score; the bare-ground mask is the precondition.

criteria_groups.name: Material and environment
criteria_groups.summary: Rock, dryness, frozen ground, temperature, radar roughness, boulders and ice. None is scored. Dryness, permafrost and temperature are measured and shown; radar is shown as RADARSAT-1 texture on Earth and Mini-RF values on the Moon, without a numerical comparison; for the others only lunar data or no data is used.

criteria_groups.name: Not reproducible on Earth
criteria_groups.summary: Conditions no natural place on Earth has. They are stated in every site's list of breaks and never scored.

criteria_groups.name: Added during the build
criteria_groups.summary: Things the pipeline computes or the app shows that the catalogue did not list: the dune-field flag, the score and ranking key, the per-region lunar targets, further context layers and the checks of the method.

criteria.name: Bare-ground mask
criteria.plain: Only ground without forest, water, ice or buildings can be a candidate, because the elevation model measures the top of whatever covers the ground.
criteria.definition: A precondition, not a feature. A cell of about 2 km can be a candidate only if at least 80% of it is bare ground, under 5% is snow or ice and under 5% is water.
criteria.dimension: Geology, mineralogy and surface materials
criteria.status_note: Implemented as catalogued. ESA WorldCover classes 'bare / sparse' (60) and 'moss and lichen' (100) count as bare, so Arctic tundra passes: without class 100, 8 of the top 30 sites keep a 4-cell core (data/validation/landcover_sensitivity.json · top30.pass_strict_cells) and 30 of the top 100 (top100.pass_strict_cells). Cells without land cover (north of 82.75 N and Antarctica) can never be candidates (data/validation/effectiveness.json · scan.land_cover_limit). A NASA variant with MODIS MCD12Q1 land cover exists and is used only in the cross-check of the second elevation model. With the mask, the four negative-control tiles give zero candidate cells (effectiveness.json · controls.*.with_mask.cells).
criteria.moon_data: Not applicable: the Moon has no land cover.
criteria.earth_data: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 (10 m); MODIS MCD12Q1 v061 through NASA GIBS for the NASA variant
criteria.comparability: One-sided: it removes Earth cells the Moon has no counterpart for. Of the known analog tiles, 9 have no bare cell and 6 have fewer than 100, so they cannot enter the tile-recovery test (effectiveness.json · recovery.known_tiles_without_bare, recovery.known_tiles_below_min_bare).
criteria.evidence: pipeline/score.py: candidate_mask, BARE_MIN = 0.8, ICE_MAX = 0.05, WATER_MAX = 0.05; pipeline/landcover.py: GROUPS

sources.label: ESA WorldCover 2021 (URL from docs/METHOD.md)
NASA GIBS, MODIS MCD12Q1 land cover (URL from docs/METHOD.md)
Copernicus DEM Product Handbook v5.0

criteria.name: Roughness spectrum
criteria.plain: How bumpy the ground is at four sizes, from 200 m to 1.6 km.
criteria.definition: Catalogue: slope of a fitted plane and roughness as 1.48 x the median absolute deviation of the height residuals, in a disc of 200, 400, 800 and 1,600 m. Built: roughness as 1.4826 x the median absolute difference between the elevation and its moving mean over a window of each of the four sizes, per cell.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Four of the eight scored features (r200, r400, r800, r1600). The detrending uses a moving mean, not NASA's plane fit, and the plane-fit slope is not a scored feature. The plane-fit estimator was written only for the check against NASA's own map: median absolute slope difference 0.042 deg on the 20 m grid and 0.064 deg at 30 m; roughness comes out at 0.84 of NASA's (docs/HANDOFF.md, section 6). The 100 m size is not built. The site records carry r200 and r1600 only; the lunar records carry all four.
criteria.moon_data: LOLA south-pole elevation model LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ at 20 m, averaged to 30 m (NASA PGDA product 90); NASA maps LDRM_80S_50MPP_ADJ_SLP_200M and _ROUGH_200M for the check
criteria.earth_data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (30 m surface model)
criteria.comparability: Same code on both bodies. Caveat: the lunar grid is partly interpolated between laser tracks and the Earth model includes vegetation and smooths small landforms; the 200 m roughness differs between two Earth elevation models (docs/METHOD.md).
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py: SCORED, ROUGH_WINDOWS_M, cell_features; validation/t1_reproduce.py; data/validation/t1_reproduce_nasa.json

sources.label: NASA PGDA product 90, LOLA south-pole products (Barker et al. 2023)
Barker et al. 2023, Planet. Sci. J. 4, 183 (preprint)
Copernicus DEM Product Handbook v5.0

criteria.name: Distance between slope distributions
criteria.plain: Compare the whole spread of slopes in a place, not only the typical slope.
criteria.definition: Wasserstein-1 distance between the slope histograms of an Earth cell and of the lunar target, per baseline.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: No code computes a Wasserstein distance or any histogram distance. The score uses the Mahalanobis distance of eight per-cell medians and shares instead.
criteria.moon_data: Would use the slope histograms of A1
criteria.earth_data: Would use the slope histograms of A1
criteria.comparability: Not tested here. The catalogue itself marks the choice of this distance as the researchers' reasoning, not a published method.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py and pipeline/score.py contain no histogram distance (searched for 'wasserstein' in pipeline/, validation/, lidar/)

sources.label: Aharonson et al. 2001, JGR 106

criteria.name: Closed depressions
criteria.plain: How much of the ground lies in hollows with no outlet, as crater floors do.
criteria.definition: Share of the cell inside closed depressions deeper than 3 m (dep_frac) and the 95th percentile of the fill depth (dep_depth), found by filling the cell with its border as the outlet.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Two of the eight scored features (dep_frac, dep_depth). The catalogue also listed depression density per km2, circularity and depth-to-diameter ratio: those are not built. Adding the two depression features to slope and roughness lowers the share of cells that pass the terrain threshold from 9.83% to 4.88% (docs/VALIDATION.md). The site records carry dep_frac; dep_depth is in the lunar records only.
criteria.moon_data: LOLA south-pole elevation model LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ at 20 m, averaged to 30 m (NASA PGDA product 90)
criteria.earth_data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (30 m surface model)
criteria.comparability: Same code on both bodies. Caveats: on Earth the detector also responds to lakes, playas, salt flats and thermokarst; the two Earth elevation models disagree on this feature (correlation 0.758, docs/VALIDATION.md), so the list of candidate cells depends on the elevation model.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py: DEP, DEP_MIN_DEPTH_M, cell_features (skimage reconstruction); data/validation/effectiveness.json: ablation

sources.label: NASA PGDA product 90, LOLA south-pole products (Barker et al. 2023)
Copernicus DEM Product Handbook v5.0

criteria.name: Drainage integration
criteria.plain: Whether water would flow out of an area along valleys or collect in hollows inside it.
criteria.definition: Share of a cell's area that drains beyond the cell against the share that drains into internal hollows.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: No flow routing is computed. The closed-depression share of A3 is the only related quantity.
criteria.moon_data: Would use the same lunar elevation model as A3
criteria.earth_data: Would use the same Earth elevation model as A3
criteria.comparability: Not tested here. The catalogue notes it has no anchor in the lunar literature.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py: no flow-direction or drainage code; the feature lists SCORED and EXTRA do not contain it

criteria.name: Anisotropy
criteria.plain: Whether the landforms line up in one direction, as valleys and ridges do, or have no preferred direction, as crater fields do.
criteria.definition: Catalogue: ratio of directional structure functions or of the eigenvalues of the surface-normal orientation tensor. Tested variant: coherence of the gradient structure tensor per cell, 0 for no preferred direction and 1 for one direction.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: One variant (gradient coherence, coh) was tested on the 37 pilot tiles and did not change which cells match: the shares with and without it are nearly the same in every tile (columns amp_all and coh_all). It is still computed as a descriptive value for the lunar cells but is not scored and is not in the site records. The two variants named in the catalogue were not built.
criteria.moon_data: LOLA south-pole elevation model LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ at 20 m, averaged to 30 m (NASA PGDA product 90)
criteria.earth_data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (30 m surface model)
criteria.comparability: Same code on both bodies, but the tested variant added no separation, so it is not used.
criteria.evidence: analysis/discovery_test_results.txt (columns amp_all, coh_all); docs/HANDOFF.md, section 6: 'Gradient coherence adds nothing'; pipeline/features.py: EXTRA

criteria.name: Two-point slope at two baselines
criteria.plain: How steep the ground typically is when measured between two points 240 m and 570 m apart.
criteria.definition: Median absolute two-point slope |h(x + b) - h(x)| / b per cell, at baselines of about 240 m and 570 m, grid rows and columns pooled.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Two of the eight scored features (s240, s570). Differences from the catalogue: baselines are 240 and 570 m (whole numbers of 30 m pixels) instead of 225 and 560 m; both grid directions are pooled instead of columns only; the lunar reference is computed by the same code from the lunar elevation model, not read from the PGDA 70 maps. PGDA 70 is used only as a check: the ratio of our grid slope to it is 1.01 to 1.03 along the north-south direction and 0.91 with both directions pooled (docs/HANDOFF.md, section 6).
criteria.moon_data: LOLA south-pole elevation model LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ at 20 m, averaged to 30 m (NASA PGDA product 90); PGDA 70 along-track slope maps for the check
criteria.earth_data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (30 m surface model)
criteria.comparability: Same code on both bodies. Caveat: a 30 m surface model includes vegetation and its noise limits baselines to about 200 m and longer.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py: SLOPE_BASELINES_M, cell_features; data/validation/t1_reproduce_nasa.json: step5_profile_vs_grid

sources.label: NASA PGDA product 70, LOLA slope and Hurst maps (Rosenburg et al. 2011)
Rosenburg et al. 2011, JGR 116, E02001
Kreslavsky and Head 2000, JGR 105
NASA PGDA product 90, LOLA south-pole products (Barker et al. 2023)

criteria.name: Engineering slope shares
criteria.plain: How much of the ground is gentle enough to land on or to walk and drive across.
criteria.definition: Share of pixels in a cell whose slope is at or below 5, 8 and 15 degrees (central-difference slope over a 2-pixel baseline, about 60 m).
criteria.dimension: Landing, mobility, navigation, operations and construction
criteria.status_note: Built in a reduced form: three thresholds (5, 8, 15 deg), shown per site and per lunar region, not scored. Not built: the 100 m erosion buffer for landing accuracy, the 20 and 25 deg classes and the largest connected traversable area. The lunar NASA slope maps at 5 m (PGDA 78 and 104) are not used; both sides are computed from the 30 m grids.
criteria.moon_data: LOLA south-pole elevation model LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ at 20 m, averaged to 30 m (NASA PGDA product 90)
criteria.earth_data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (30 m surface model)
criteria.comparability: Same code and same baseline on both bodies. Caveat: the thresholds come from requirements at the scale of a lander or rover (metres), and a slope over about 60 m is lower than the slope a vehicle meets.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py: EXTRA, cell_features (loop over 5, 8, 15); pipeline/sites.py: MEDIAN_COLS

sources.label: Kumari et al. 2022, Planet. Sci. J. 3:224
LPSC 2022 abstract 1079, 100 m landing buffer
NASA ACR24, Lunar Mobility Drivers and Needs
NASA PGDA product 78, 5 m DEMs of south-pole sites (Barker et al. 2021)
NASA PGDA product 104, 5 m DEMs of the 13 candidate regions

criteria.name: Local relief and hypsometry
criteria.plain: The height difference between the low and the high ground inside an area, and how the heights are distributed.
criteria.definition: Catalogue: 5th to 95th percentile elevation range, hypsometric integral and skewness of elevation in a window. Built: the percentile range (relief) and the median elevation per cell.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Relief (P95 - P5 of elevation per cell) and median elevation are computed on both bodies and are not scored. Relief is shown for the lunar regions and feeds the dune-field flag (D1); the site records carry the median elevation only. The hypsometric integral and the skewness are not built.
criteria.moon_data: LOLA south-pole elevation model LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ at 20 m, averaged to 30 m (NASA PGDA product 90)
criteria.earth_data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (30 m surface model)
criteria.comparability: Same code on both bodies. Absolute elevation has no common reference between the two bodies, so only relief is comparable.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py: EXTRA, cell_features (elev_med, relief); pipeline/sites.py: artefact_threshold

criteria.name: Shadow geometry at low sun
criteria.plain: How much of the terrain would lie in shadow if the sun stood as low as it does at the lunar pole.
criteria.definition: Share of terrain in shadow at sun elevations of 1.5 and 5 degrees, averaged over azimuths, from horizon rasters computed by the same code on both bodies.
criteria.dimension: Temperature, illumination and environmental extremes
criteria.status_note: No horizon or shadow code exists. What the app shows instead is not this criterion: NASA's own illumination, permanent-shadow and Earth-visibility maps per lunar region (D7), and a line in each site's list of breaks giving the midsummer noon sun elevation from the site's latitude.
criteria.moon_data: NASA PGDA product 69 would have been the check; it is used only as lunar context (D7)
criteria.earth_data: None
criteria.comparability: Not tested here. The catalogue warns that the result depends strongly on the resolution of the elevation model and that no place on Earth has lunar illumination.
criteria.evidence: No horizon code in pipeline/, validation/ or lidar/; pipeline/sites.py: breaks_for, noon_sun_deg

sources.label: NASA PGDA product 69, polar illumination (Mazarico et al. 2011)
Glaeser et al. 2018, illumination of the lunar poles

criteria.name: Differential slope and profile curvature
criteria.plain: Slope with the regional tilt removed, and how sharply the ground bends.
criteria.definition: Differential slope s(L) - s(2L) and the interquartile range of profile curvature at baselines from 115 m to 1.8 km (after Kreslavsky).
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Not implemented. The catalogue itself notes that the formulas were written from memory and not checked against the papers.
criteria.moon_data: Would use the lunar elevation model
criteria.earth_data: Would use the Earth elevation model
criteria.comparability: Not tested here.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/features.py: SCORED and EXTRA contain no differential slope or curvature

sources.label: Kreslavsky et al. 2013, Icarus 226
Kreslavsky and Head 2000, JGR 105

criteria.name: ICESat-2 laser profiles
criteria.plain: Check the slopes from the 30 m elevation model against a satellite laser that measures the ground along a line, as the lunar laser altimeter does.
criteria.definition: Median absolute point-to-point slope along ICESat-2 ground tracks at 60, 220, 240 and 560 m, compared with the grid slopes of the same site and with the lunar values.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Run for eight sites, not for the ranking. The laser slope at 240 m is 0.43 to 1.16 times the grid slope, median 0.87 (data/validation/icesat2.json · sites.*.ratios.laser240_over_grid240); the three lowest are lava fields. Differences from the catalogue: the standard ATL06 product (heights fitted over 40 m segments, posted every 20 m) is used, so 60 m stands in for the 57 m lunar baseline, and the laser samples a square box of 10 x 10 km (half-size 5 km) around the site centre, not the site outline (icesat2.json · request.aoi).
criteria.moon_data: NASA PGDA product 70 along-track medians; our lunar grid medians
criteria.earth_data: ICESat-2 ATL06 (NASA) through SlideRule Earth; Copernicus DEM GLO-30 for the grid side
criteria.comparability: The only Earth measurement with the same geometry as the lunar laser altimeter. Caveat: 40 m segment averages against laser spots of about 5 m on the Moon, different track directions and different footprints.
criteria.evidence: validation/icesat2_profiles.py; data/validation/icesat2.json: sites.*.ratios.laser240_over_grid240; docs/VALIDATION.md

sources.label: SlideRule Earth, public cluster
NASA PGDA product 70, LOLA slope and Hurst maps (Rosenburg et al. 2011)
NASA Earthdata Search (URL from docs/METHOD.md)

criteria.name: Airborne lidar close-ups at 1 m
criteria.plain: Look at a few places with a far sharper elevation model to see what the 30 m model loses.
criteria.definition: Catalogue: the A1 estimator on 1 m lidar terrain models averaged to 20 m, also at a 100 m baseline. Built: crater shape (rim diameter, depth, rim height, wall slope) from radial profiles on 1 m lidar, on the 30 m model and on the lunar 20 m model.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Built as a crater close-up, not as the roughness estimator the catalogue describes. Meteor Crater on 1 m lidar: rim-crest diameter 1,222 m, depth 163 m; the 30 m model keeps size and depth (1,258 m, 162 m) and loses the steep walls (steepest profile slope 36.8 deg against 40.7 deg). A lunar crater of 1,140 m from the 20 m model is the comparison. The Morasko craters in Poland (1 m lidar) are a counter-example, not an analog: they are not resolved at 30 m. ArcticDEM is not used.
criteria.moon_data: LOLA south-pole elevation model at 20 m (NASA PGDA product 90)
criteria.earth_data: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar (Meteor Crater); GUGiK NMT 1 m (Morasko, Poland); Copernicus DEM GLO-30
criteria.comparability: Two craters and one counter-example only; it shows the limits of the 30 m model and does not enter the ranking.
criteria.evidence: lidar/crater_profiles.py; data/validation/crater_profiles.json: a_meteor_3dep_1m, b_meteor_glo30, c_moon_lola_20m, d_morasko

sources.label: USGS 3DEP 1 m, S3 listing
GUGiK, numerical terrain model (Poland)
NASA PGDA product 90, LOLA south-pole products (Barker et al. 2023)

criteria.name: Landform classes (geomorphons)
criteria.plain: Classify every point as a pit, valley, ridge, peak and so on, and compare the mix of classes.
criteria.definition: Share of each geomorphon class per cell, in particular pits against valleys, with the same search distance in metres on both bodies.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Not implemented. The catalogue found no use of geomorphons on lunar elevation models and marks the idea as untested.
criteria.moon_data: Would use the lunar elevation model
criteria.earth_data: Would use the Earth elevation model
criteria.comparability: Not tested here.
criteria.evidence: No geomorphon code in pipeline/, validation/ or lidar/ (searched for 'geomorphon')

criteria.name: Hurst exponent and power-spectrum slope
criteria.plain: A single number for how roughness changes with scale.
criteria.definition: Hurst exponent fitted to the structure function of elevation over a range of distances, or the slope of the power spectrum.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Tested in the pilot and dropped. From the 30 m Earth model the value was unstable (for Meteor Crater 0.40 or 0.83 depending on the window), and at the lunar south pole it has a median of 0.98, so it separates nothing. Not computed by the pipeline.
criteria.moon_data: NASA PGDA product 70 Hurst map; Hurst layer of PGDA product 90
criteria.earth_data: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (pilot test only)
criteria.comparability: Low: too few octaves of scale in a 30 m model, opposite biases from smoothing and noise, and saturation near 1 at the pole.

criteria.name: Dune-field flag
criteria.plain: Sand seas can have lunar-like slopes and hollows; a terrain rule marks such sites and moves them to the end of the ranking.
criteria.definition: A cell is flagged when its relief divided by its 200 m roughness is below the 5th percentile of the same ratio over the lunar cells of the target; a site is flagged when at least half of its cells are.
criteria.dimension: Dust, wind, erosion and surface processes
criteria.status_note: Not part of the similarity score and not a mask: flagged sites are kept and ranked after all unflagged sites. The threshold comes from the lunar cells, not from Earth data. 521 of the 3,175 sites carry the flag (app/data/meta.json · counts.sites_flagged_total). It is a terrain rule: a check against surface temperature and soil moisture did not confirm that it marks dry sand (docs/sources/j26.md; data/validation/partner_checks.json · comparisons.dune_flag), and it also flags N75W090-01 on Devon Island, a known analog.
criteria.moon_data: Relief and 200 m roughness of the lunar target cells (data/moon/cells.parquet)
criteria.earth_data: Relief and 200 m roughness of the Earth cells (Copernicus DEM GLO-30)
criteria.comparability: Same two quantities on both bodies; by construction 5% of the target's own lunar cells would be flagged.
criteria.evidence: pipeline/sites.py: ARTEFACT_QUANTILE, ARTEFACT_SITE_SHARE, artefact_threshold, artefact_flags, rank_sites; validation/partner_checks.py

criteria.name: Similarity score and best 15 km window
criteria.plain: How the eight terrain numbers become one score per cell, and how cells become a ranked site.
criteria.definition: Per cell: Mahalanobis distance of the eight transformed features to the lunar target, turned into p_all, the share of the target's own cells that lie farther from its centre; a candidate cell has p_all of at least 0.10 and passes the mask. Touching candidate cells (at least 4) form a site. Sites are ranked by the largest sum of p_all times cell area inside any 15 x 15 km window, the size of a lunar candidate region.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: This is the aggregation of A1, A3 and A6, not a further terrain measurement. The site's 'score' is the median p_all of its cells; score_amp and score_dep are the same for the slope and roughness group and for the depression group, for display only. The best-window key replaced total similarity-weighted area because total area rewarded sheer size (docs/METHOD.md). Exact site ranks move with the grid: 6 of the top 10 survive a half-cell shift on the older 37-tile pilot subset with the old polar target (data/validation/effectiveness.json · stability.legacy_grid.variants.0.top10_overlap = 0.6). Rank uncertainty per site (issue #18) is not produced yet.
criteria.moon_data: Lunar reference populations in data/moon/reference.json
criteria.earth_data: Scored Earth cells
criteria.comparability: The depression features are zero-inflated, so the Gaussian distance is an approximation (pipeline/score.py).
criteria.evidence: pipeline/score.py: score_cells, P_MIN, candidate_mask; pipeline/sites.py: MIN_CELLS, BASE_REGION_KM, best_window, DEFAULT_RANK_KEY, rank_sites

The pooled target is a choice of definition: the validation does not separate it from the polar window (docs/METHOD.md). The windows are centred on gazetteer feature centres or on points from the cited papers, not on official region outlines.

criteria.earth_data: Not applicable
criteria.comparability: The named regions are steeper than the polar average (median slope at 240 m 7.0 deg against 5.1 deg, docs/METHOD.md), so the choice of target changes which Earth sites match.

criteria.name: Recovery of known analog sites
criteria.plain: Does the score find more lunar-like ground around places people already use as analogs than around random places?
criteria.definition: Enrichment: the share of bare cells that are candidates inside the radius of a known analog site, divided by the same share over all scanned bare cells, compared with random circles of the same radii. Also negative-control tiles and a tile-level recovery curve.
criteria.dimension: Terrain, elevation, slope, roughness and craters
criteria.status_note: Enrichment around the 22 known lunar analogs (rows tagged moon or both; Mars-only rows excluded since issue #16): median 1.02 against 0.39 for matched random circles (5th to 95th percentile 0.12 to 0.91), 11 of 22 above 1, and 2.8% of 500 random runs reach our median (data/validation/enrichment.json · median_enrichment, random.median_enrichment_median, random.share_of_random_runs_with_median_at_least_ours). The typical known lunar site sits at about the scan-wide rate. At one-degree tile scale the tile-recovery AUC is 0.531 (90% interval 0.396 to 0.668), consistent with chance (effectiveness.json · recovery.auc, recovery.auc_ci90). The score finds terrain of a certain shape; it is not a detector of the sites people chose.
criteria.moon_data: Lunar target as in D3
criteria.earth_data: Scored Earth cells; data/reference/known_analogs.csv
criteria.comparability: A test of the method, not a property of a site.
criteria.evidence: validation/enrichment.py; validation/effectiveness.py; data/validation/enrichment.json; data/validation/effectiveness.json: controls, recovery
